98: HOLDS_AT_RE = re.compile(r"holdsAt\(\s*([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)\s*\)")
99: 
100: 
101: def load_state(round_number):
102:     return {
103:         "config": json.loads((ROOT / "state" / "config.json").read_text()),
104:         "fluents": json.loads((ROOT / "state" / "fluents.json").read_text()),
105:         # Point-in-time occurrences (engine.institution.events) — distinct
106:         # from fluents.json's own interval facts; see that module's own
107:         # docstring for why the two are kept apart.
108:         "events": json.loads((ROOT / "state" / "events.json").read_text()),
109:         "runtime": json.loads((ROOT / "state" / "runtime.json").read_text()),
110:         "agents": json.loads((ROOT / "constants" / "agents.json").read_text()),
111:         # Object TYPE definitions are auto-discovered by scanning
112:         # state/object_types/*.json directly (keyed by each file's own
113:         # type_name) — same "the directory itself is the source of truth,
114:         # institution.json is drift-checked documentation, never the load
115:         # path" principle actions/rules/*/*.py already uses. Object INSTANCE
116:         # declarations (id/type only — never mutable field values, see
117:         # engine/institution/objects.py's own module docstring) come from
118:         # state/objects.json.
119:         "object_types": load_object_types(),
120:         "objects": load_objects(),
121:         "round_number": round_number,
122:     }
123: 
124: 
125: def load_object_types():
126:     types = {}
127:     for path in sorted((ROOT / "state" / "object_types").glob("*.json")):
128:         spec = json.loads(path.read_text())
129:         types[spec["type_name"]] = spec
130:     return types
131: 
132: 
133: def load_objects():
134:     return json.loads((ROOT / "state" / "objects.json").read_text())
135: 
136: 
137: def load_action_spec(action_name):
138:     """state/actions/{action_name}.json — loaded by filename-stem
139:     convention (action_name == the state/schedule.json key == the spec's
140:     own "name" field), never indirected through institution.json's own
141:     "spec" field, which stays purely informational/drift-checked (see
142:     norm_implementation_institution_errors()) rather than a live load
143:     path — the same relationship institution.json already has with
144:     actions/rules/**/*.py and state/object_types/*.json."""
145:     return json.loads((ROOT / "state" / "actions" / f"{action_name}.json").read_text())
146: 
147: 
148: def load_institution():
149:     return json.loads((ROOT / "state" / "institution.json").read_text())
150: 
151: 
152: def load_schedule():
153:     return json.loads((ROOT / "state" / "schedule.json").read_text())
154: 
155: 
156: def compile_and_write_schedule():
157:     """Regenerates state/schedule.json from state/institution.json's own
158:     action catalog plus each state/actions/*.json's own
159:     scheduling.after/before/gate — schedule.json is now a COMPILED
160:     artifact (engine.institution.scheduler.compile_schedule()), never
161:     hand-edited, so a norm-implementer round that added or reordered an
162:     action can never leave it silently out of sync with institution.json
163:     (a whole bug class the old hand-maintained file had no check for at
164:     all). Called at the top of every round, and once before main()'s own
165:     initial read, so this is always fresh before anything reads it."""
166:     institution = load_institution()
167:     action_specs = {name: load_action_spec(name) for name in institution.get("actions", {})}
168:     schedule = compile_schedule(action_specs)
169:     (ROOT / "state" / "schedule.json").write_text(json.dumps(schedule, indent=2) + "\n")
170:     return schedule
171: 
172: 
173: def evaluate_gate(condition, fluents, round_number):
174:     """Supported syntax: "true", "false", or "holdsAt(<fluent_name>)" — true
175:     if any record for that fluent (any holder/args) is currently active."""
176:     condition = condition.strip()
177:     if condition == "true":
178:         return True
179:     if condition == "false":
180:         return False
181: 
182:     match = HOLDS_AT_RE.fullmatch(condition)
183:     if not match:
184:         raise ValueError(f"unsupported state/schedule.json gate condition: {condition!r}")
185: 
186:     fluent_name = match.group(1)
187:     return any(
188:         f["fluent"] == fluent_name
189:         and f["initiated_round"] <= round_number
190:         and (f["terminated_round"] is None or f["terminated_round"] > round_number)
191:         for f in fluents
192:     )

# /understand

Analyze the current codebase and produce a `knowledge-graph.json` file in the project's data directory (`.ua/`, or the legacy `.understand-anything/` when it already exists). This file powers the interactive dashboard for exploring the project's architecture.

## Options

- `$ARGUMENTS` may contain:
  - `--full` — Force a full rebuild, ignoring any existing graph
  - `--auto-update` — Enable automatic graph updates on commit (writes `autoUpdate: true` to `$UA_DIR/config.json`)
  - `--no-auto-update` — Disable automatic graph updates (writes `autoUpdate: false` to `$UA_DIR/config.json`)
  - `--review` — Run full LLM graph-reviewer instead of inline deterministic validation
  - `--language <lang>` — Generate all textual content (summaries, descriptions, tags, titles, languageNotes, languageLesson) in the specified language. Accepts ISO 639-1 codes (`zh`, `ja`, `ko`, `en`, `es`, `fr`, `de`, etc.) or friendly names (`chinese`, `japanese`, `korean`, `english`, `spanish`, etc.). Locale variants supported: `zh-TW`, `zh-HK`, etc. Defaults to `en` (English). Stores preference in `$UA_DIR/config.json` for consistency across incremental updates.
  - `--exclude <patterns>` — Comma-separated glob patterns for additional files/directories to exclude from analysis (e.g., `--exclude "tests/*,docs/*"`). These patterns take highest priority over built-in defaults and `.understandignore` rules. Supports gitignore syntax including `!` negation.
  - A directory path (e.g. `/path/to/repo` or `../other-project`) — Analyze the given directory instead of the current working directory

---

## Progress Reporting

Throughout execution, report progress to the user at each phase transition and during batch processing. This keeps users informed on large codebases where analysis can take a long time.

- **Phase transitions:** At the start of each phase, print a status line:
  > `[Phase N/7] <phase name>...`

- **Batch progress:** During Phase 2, report each batch with its index and total:

- **Phase completion:** When a phase finishes, briefly confirm:
  > `Phase N complete. <one-line summary of result>`
  >

   - **Worktree redirect.** If `PROJECT_ROOT` is inside a git worktree (not the main checkout), redirect output to the main repository root. Worktrees managed by Claude Code are ephemeral — the data directory (`.ua/`, or legacy `.understand-anything/`) written there is destroyed when the session ends, taking the knowledge graph with it (issue #133). Detect a worktree by comparing `git rev-parse --git-dir` against `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`; in a normal checkout or submodule they resolve to the same path, in a worktree they differ and the parent of `--git-common-dir` is the main repo root.

     ```bash
     COMMON_DIR=$(git -C "$PROJECT_ROOT" rev-parse --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null)
     GIT_DIR=$(git -C "$PROJECT_ROOT" rev-parse --git-dir 2>/dev/null)
     if [ -n "$COMMON_DIR" ] && [ -n "$GIT_DIR" ]; then
       COMMON_ABS=$(cd "$PROJECT_ROOT" && cd "$COMMON_DIR" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
       GIT_ABS=$(cd "$PROJECT_ROOT" && cd "$GIT_DIR" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
       if [ -n "$COMMON_ABS" ] && [ "$COMMON_ABS" != "$GIT_ABS" ]; then
         MAIN_ROOT=$(dirname "$COMMON_ABS")
         if [ -d "$MAIN_ROOT" ] && [ "${UNDERSTAND_NO_WORKTREE_REDIRECT:-0}" != "1" ]; then
           echo "[understand] Detected git worktree at $PROJECT_ROOT"
           echo "[understand] Redirecting output to main repo root: $MAIN_ROOT"
           echo "[understand] (Set UNDERSTAND_NO_WORKTREE_REDIRECT=1 to keep PROJECT_ROOT as the worktree.)"
           PROJECT_ROOT="$MAIN_ROOT"
         fi
       fi
     fi
     ```

     Set `UNDERSTAND_NO_WORKTREE_REDIRECT=1` if you intentionally want a per-worktree graph (rare — most users want the redirect).
1.5. **Ensure the plugin is built.** Later phases invoke Node scripts that import `@understand-anything/core`. On a fresh install `packages/core/dist/` does not exist yet — build once.

   **Important:** do **not** assume the plugin root is simply two directories above the skill path string. In many installations `~/.agents/skills/understand` is a symlink into the real plugin checkout. Prefer runtime-provided plugin roots first (for Claude), then fall back to universal symlinks, skill symlink resolution, and common clone-based install paths.

   Resolve the plugin root like this:

   ```bash
   SKILL_REAL=$(realpath ~/.agents/skills/understand 2>/dev/null || readlink -f ~/.agents/skills/understand 2>/dev/null || echo "")
   SELF_RELATIVE=$([ -n "$SKILL_REAL" ] && cd "$SKILL_REAL/../.." 2>/dev/null && pwd || echo "")
   COPILOT_SKILL_REAL=$(realpath ~/.copilot/skills/understand 2>/dev/null || readlink -f ~/.copilot/skills/understand 2>/dev/null || echo "")
   COPILOT_SELF_RELATIVE=$([ -n "$COPILOT_SKILL_REAL" ] && cd "$COPILOT_SKILL_REAL/../.." 2>/dev/null && pwd || echo "")

   PLUGIN_ROOT=""
   for candidate in \
     "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}" \
     "$HOME/.understand-anything-plugin" \
     "$SELF_RELATIVE" \
     "$COPILOT_SELF_RELATIVE" \
     "$HOME/.codex/understand-anything/understand-anything-plugin" \
     "$HOME/.opencode/understand-anything/understand-anything-plugin" \
     "$HOME/.pi/understand-anything/understand-anything-plugin" \
     "$HOME/understand-anything/understand-anything-plugin"; do
     if [ -n "$candidate" ] && [ -f "$candidate/package.json" ] && [ -f "$candidate/pnpm-workspace.yaml" ]; then
       PLUGIN_ROOT="$candidate"
       break
     fi
   done

   if [ -z "$PLUGIN_ROOT" ]; then
     echo "Error: Cannot find the understand-anything plugin root."
     echo "Checked:"
     echo "  - ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-<unset CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT>}"
     echo "  - $HOME/.understand-anything-plugin"
     echo "  - ${SELF_RELATIVE:-<unresolved path derived from ~/.agents/skills/understand>}"
     echo "  - ${COPILOT_SELF_RELATIVE:-<unresolved path derived from ~/.copilot/skills/understand>}"
     echo "  - $HOME/.codex/understand-anything/understand-anything-plugin"
     echo "  - $HOME/.opencode/understand-anything/understand-anything-plugin"
     echo "  - $HOME/.pi/understand-anything/understand-anything-plugin"
     echo "  - $HOME/understand-anything/understand-anything-plugin"
     echo "Make sure the plugin is installed correctly."
     exit 1
   fi

   if [ ! -f "$PLUGIN_ROOT/packages/core/dist/index.js" ]; then
     cd "$PLUGIN_ROOT" && (pnpm install --frozen-lockfile 2>/dev/null || pnpm install) && pnpm --filter @understand-anything/core build
   fi
   ```

The merge script's regex (`batch-(\d+)(?:-part-(\d+))?\.json`) silently drops any other naming (e.g., `batch-fused-8-13.json`, `batch-8-13.json`), losing every node and edge in that file. After each dispatch returns, verify each `batchIndex` in the dispatched input has a corresponding `batch-<batchIndex>.json` (or `batch-<batchIndex>-part-*.json`) on disk before proceeding to the next dispatch.

After ALL batches complete, report to the user: `Phase 2 complete. All <totalBatches> batches analyzed.`

Run the merge-and-normalize script bundled with this skill (located next to this SKILL.md file — use the skill directory path, not the project root):
```bash
python "<SKILL_DIR>/merge-batch-graphs.py" "$PROJECT_ROOT"
```

This script reads all `batch-*.json` files (including `batch-<i>-part-<k>.json` produced by file-analyzers that split their output) from `$UA_DIR/intermediate/`, then in one pass:
- Combines all nodes and edges across batches
- Normalizes node IDs (strips double prefixes, project-name prefixes, adds missing prefixes)
- Normalizes complexity values (`low`→`simple`, `medium`→`moderate`, `high`→`complex`, etc.)
- Rewrites edge references to match corrected node IDs
- Deduplicates nodes by ID (keeps last occurrence) and edges by `(source, target, type)`
- Drops dangling edges referencing missing nodes
- Logs all corrections and dropped items to stderr

The merge script also runs a `tested_by` linker that canonicalizes test-coverage edges in two passes. **Pass 1** walks LLM-emitted `tested_by` edges and flips inverted ones in place; semantically broken edges (test↔test, prod↔prod, orphan endpoints) are dropped. **Pass 2** supplements with path-convention pairings. Production nodes that end up sourcing any `tested_by` edge get a `"tested"` tag. All resulting edges run `production → test`.

Output: `$UA_DIR/intermediate/assembled-graph.json`

Include the script's warnings in `$PHASE_WARNINGS` for the reviewer.

#### Default path (no `--review`): inline deterministic validation

Write the following Node.js script to `$UA_DIR/tmp/ua-inline-validate.cjs`:

```javascript
#!/usr/bin/env node
const fs = require('fs');
const graphPath = process.argv[2];
const outputPath = process.argv[3];
try {
  const graph = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(graphPath, 'utf8'));
  const issues = [], warnings = [];
  if (!Array.isArray(graph.nodes)) { issues.push('graph.nodes is missing or not an array'); graph.nodes = []; }
  if (!Array.isArray(graph.edges)) { issues.push('graph.edges is missing or not an array'); graph.edges = []; }
  const nodeIds = new Set();
  const seen = new Map();
  graph.nodes.forEach((n, i) => {
    if (!n.id) { issues.push(`Node[${i}] missing id`); return; }
    if (!n.type) issues.push(`Node[${i}] '${n.id}' missing type`);
    if (!n.name) issues.push(`Node[${i}] '${n.id}' missing name`);
    if (!n.summary) issues.push(`Node[${i}] '${n.id}' missing summary`);
    if (!n.tags || !n.tags.length) issues.push(`Node[${i}] '${n.id}' missing tags`);
    if (seen.has(n.id)) issues.push(`Duplicate node ID '${n.id}' at indices ${seen.get(n.id)} and ${i}`);
    else seen.set(n.id, i);
    nodeIds.add(n.id);
  });
  graph.edges.forEach((e, i) => {
    if (!nodeIds.has(e.source)) issues.push(`Edge[${i}] source '${e.source}' not found`);
    if (!nodeIds.has(e.target)) issues.push(`Edge[${i}] target '${e.target}' not found`);
  });
  const fileLevelTypes = new Set(['file', 'config', 'document', 'service', 'pipeline', 'table', 'schema', 'resource', 'endpoint']);
  const fileNodes = graph.nodes.filter(n => fileLevelTypes.has(n.type)).map(n => n.id);
  const assigned = new Map();
  if (!Array.isArray(graph.layers)) { if (graph.layers) warnings.push('graph.layers is not an array'); graph.layers = []; }
  if (!Array.isArray(graph.tour)) { if (graph.tour) warnings.push('graph.tour is not an array'); graph.tour = []; }
  graph.layers.forEach(layer => {
    (layer.nodeIds || []).forEach(id => {
      if (!nodeIds.has(id)) issues.push(`Layer '${layer.id}' refs missing node '${id}'`);
      if (assigned.has(id)) issues.push(`Node '${id}' appears in multiple layers`);
      assigned.set(id, layer.id);
    });
  });
  fileNodes.forEach(id => {
    if (!assigned.has(id)) issues.push(`File node '${id}' not in any layer`);
  });
  graph.tour.forEach((step, i) => {
    (step.nodeIds || []).forEach(id => {
      if (!nodeIds.has(id)) issues.push(`Tour step[${i}] refs missing node '${id}'`);
    });
  });
  const withEdges = new Set([
    ...graph.edges.map(e => e.source),
    ...graph.edges.map(e => e.target)
  ]);
  graph.nodes.forEach(n => {
    if (!withEdges.has(n.id)) warnings.push(`Node '${n.id}' has no edges (orphan)`);
  });
  const stats = {
    totalNodes: graph.nodes.length,
    totalEdges: graph.edges.length,
    totalLayers: graph.layers.length,
    tourSteps: graph.tour.length,
    nodeTypes: graph.nodes.reduce((a, n) => { a[n.type] = (a[n.type]||0)+1; return a; }, {}),
    edgeTypes: graph.edges.reduce((a, e) => { a[e.type] = (a[e.type]||0)+1; return a; }, {})
  };
  fs.writeFileSync(outputPath, JSON.stringify({ issues, warnings, stats }, null, 2));
  process.exit(0);
} catch (err) { process.stderr.write(err.message + '\n'); process.exit(1); }
```

   Write the input file:
   ```bash
   node - "$PROJECT_ROOT" "$UA_DIR/intermediate/fingerprint-input.json" <<'NODE'
   const fs = require('fs');
   const projectRoot = process.argv[2];
   const outputPath = process.argv[3];

     projectRoot,
     sourceFilePaths: [<all source file paths from Phase 1, as JSON array>],
     gitCommitHash: "<current commit hash>",
   };

   ```bash

     "$UA_DIR/intermediate/fingerprint-input.json"
   ```

   The script uses `TreeSitterPlugin + PluginRegistry` exactly like `extract-structure.mjs`, so the baseline matches the comparison logic used during auto-updates.

3. Write metadata to `$UA_DIR/meta.json` (only after step 2 succeeded):
   ```json

     "analyzedFiles": <number of files analyzed>
   }
   ```

4. Clean up intermediate files, **preserving `scan-result.json`** so future incremental runs can skip Phase 1 SCAN (see issue #293). We `mv` scratch dirs into a timestamped `.trash-*` instead of `rm -rf`ing them directly — this avoids tripping destructive-action gates on hardened hosts (e.g. freshness-window checks) that flag deleting directories created moments earlier (see issue #301). The delayed-purge step in Phase 0 reclaims the space once the trash is older than 7 days.
   ```bash
   # Preserve scan-result.json — Phase 1's deterministic file inventory.
   # Future incremental runs (Phase 2 compute-batches.mjs --changed-files=…)
   # need this inventory; without it, Phase 1 must re-dispatch and pay ~157k
   # tokens / ~158s per incremental run.
   TRASH="$UA_DIR/.trash-$(date +%s)"
   mkdir -p "$TRASH"
   INTER="$UA_DIR/intermediate"
   if [ -d "$INTER" ]; then
     # Move every entry except scan-result.json into the trash dir.
     find "$INTER" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -not -name 'scan-result.json' -exec mv {} "$TRASH/" \; 2>/dev/null || true
   fi
   mv "$UA_DIR/tmp" "$TRASH/" 2>/dev/null || true
   ```

# Skill: understand

# /understand

Analyze the current codebase and produce a `knowledge-graph.json` file in the project's data directory (`.ua/`, or the legacy `.understand-anything/` when it already exists). This file powers the interactive dashboard for exploring the project's architecture.

## Options

- `$ARGUMENTS` may contain:
  - `--full` — Force a full rebuild, ignoring any existing graph
  - `--auto-update` — Enable automatic graph updates on commit (writes `autoUpdate: true` to `$UA_DIR/config.json`)
  - `--no-auto-update` — Disable automatic graph updates (writes `autoUpdate: false` to `$UA_DIR/config.json`)
  - `--review` — Run full LLM graph-reviewer instead of inline deterministic validation
  - `--language <lang>` — Generate all textual content (summaries, descriptions, tags, titles, languageNotes, languageLesson) in the specified language. Accepts ISO 639-1 codes (`zh`, `ja`, `ko`, `en`, `es`, `fr`, `de`, etc.) or friendly names (`chinese`, `japanese`, `korean`, `english`, `spanish`, etc.). Locale variants supported: `zh-TW`, `zh-HK`, etc. Defaults to `en` (English). Stores preference in `$UA_DIR/config.json` for consistency across incremental updates.
  - `--exclude <patterns>` — Comma-separated glob patterns for additional files/directories to exclude from analysis (e.g., `--exclude "tests/*,docs/*"`). These patterns take highest priority over built-in defaults and `.understandignore` rules. Supports gitignore syntax including `!` negation.
  - A directory path (e.g. `/path/to/repo` or `../other-project`) — Analyze the given directory instead of the current working directory

---

## Progress Reporting

Throughout execution, report progress to the user at each phase transition and during batch processing. This keeps users informed on large codebases where analysis can take a long time.

- **Phase transitions:** At the start of each phase, print a status line:
  > `[Phase N/7] <phase name>...`
  >
  > Example: `[Phase 2/7] Analyzing files (12 batches)...`

- **Batch progress:** During Phase 2, report each batch with its index and total:
  > `Analyzing batch X/N (files: foo.ts, bar.ts, ...)` (list up to 3 filenames, then `...` if more)

- **Phase completion:** When a phase finishes, briefly confirm:
  > `Phase N complete. <one-line summary of result>`
  >
  > Example: `Phase 1 complete. Found 247 files across 3 languages.`

#### Default path (no `--review`): inline deterministic validation

Write the following Node.js script to `$UA_DIR/tmp/ua-inline-validate.cjs`:

```javascript
#!/usr/bin/env node
const fs = require('fs');
const graphPath = process.argv[2];
const outputPath = process.argv[3];
try {
  const graph = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(graphPath, 'utf8'));
  const issues = [], warnings = [];
  if (!Array.isArray(graph.nodes)) { issues.push('graph.nodes is missing or not an array'); graph.nodes = []; }
  if (!Array.isArray(graph.edges)) { issues.push('graph.edges is missing or not an array'); graph.edges = []; }
  const nodeIds = new Set();
  const seen = new Map();
  graph.nodes.forEach((n, i) => {
    if (!n.id) { issues.push(`Node[${i}] missing id`); return; }
    if (!n.type) issues.push(`Node[${i}] '${n.id}' missing type`);
    if (!n.name) issues.push(`Node[${i}] '${n.id}' missing name`);
    if (!n.summary) issues.push(`Node[${i}] '${n.id}' missing summary`);
    if (!n.tags || !n.tags.length) issues.push(`Node[${i}] '${n.id}' missing tags`);
    if (seen.has(n.id)) issues.push(`Duplicate node ID '${n.id}' at indices ${seen.get(n.id)} and ${i}`);
    else seen.set(n.id, i);
    nodeIds.add(n.id);
  });
  graph.edges.forEach((e, i) => {
    if (!nodeIds.has(e.source)) issues.push(`Edge[${i}] source '${e.source}' not found`);
    if (!nodeIds.has(e.target)) issues.push(`Edge[${i}] target '${e.target}' not found`);
  });
  const fileLevelTypes = new Set(['file', 'config', 'document', 'service', 'pipeline', 'table', 'schema', 'resource', 'endpoint']);
  const fileNodes = graph.nodes.filter(n => fileLevelTypes.has(n.type)).map(n => n.id);
  const assigned = new Map();
  if (!Array.isArray(graph.layers)) { if (graph.layers) warnings.push('graph.layers is not an array'); graph.layers = []; }
  if (!Array.isArray(graph.tour)) { if (graph.tour) warnings.push('graph.tour is not an array'); graph.tour = []; }
  graph.layers.forEach(layer => {
    (layer.nodeIds || []).forEach(id => {
      if (!nodeIds.has(id)) issues.push(`Layer '${layer.id}' refs missing node '${id}'`);
      if (assigned.has(id)) issues.push(`Node '${id}' appears in multiple layers`);
      assigned.set(id, layer.id);
    });
  });
  fileNodes.forEach(id => {
    if (!assigned.has(id)) issues.push(`File node '${id}' not in any layer`);
  });
  graph.tour.forEach((step, i) => {
    (step.nodeIds || []).forEach(id => {
      if (!nodeIds.has(id)) issues.push(`Tour step[${i}] refs missing node '${id}'`);
    });
  });
  const withEdges = new Set([
    ...graph.edges.map(e => e.source),
    ...graph.edges.map(e => e.target)
  ]);
  graph.nodes.forEach(n => {
    if (!withEdges.has(n.id)) warnings.push(`Node '${n.id}' has no edges (orphan)`);
  });
  const stats = {
    totalNodes: graph.nodes.length,
    totalEdges: graph.edges.length,
    totalLayers: graph.layers.length,
    tourSteps: graph.tour.length,
    nodeTypes: graph.nodes.reduce((a, n) => { a[n.type] = (a[n.type]||0)+1; return a; }, {}),
    edgeTypes: graph.edges.reduce((a, e) => { a[e.type] = (a[e.type]||0)+1; return a; }, {})
  };
  fs.writeFileSync(outputPath, JSON.stringify({ issues, warnings, stats }, null, 2));
  process.exit(0);
} catch (err) { process.stderr.write(err.message + '\n'); process.exit(1); }
```

We `mv` scratch dirs into a timestamped `.trash-*` instead of `rm -rf`ing them directly — this avoids tripping destructive-action gates on hardened hosts (e.g. freshness-window checks) that flag deleting directories created moments earlier (see issue #301). The delayed-purge step in Phase 0 reclaims the space once the trash is older than 7 days.
   ```bash
   # Preserve scan-result.json — Phase 1's deterministic file inventory.
   # Future incremental runs (Phase 2 compute-batches.mjs --changed-files=…)

   TRASH="$UA_DIR/.trash-$(date +%s)"
   mkdir -p "$TRASH"
   INTER="$UA_DIR/intermediate"
   if [ -d "$INTER" ]; then
     # Move every entry except scan-result.json into the trash dir.
     find "$INTER" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -not -name 'scan-result.json' -exec mv {} "$TRASH/" \; 2>/dev/null || true
   fi

1: # Round 1 Institutional Design Specification
2: 
3: ## Overview
4: Implemented the policy:
5: * Fisher records name, date, expected take before departing.
6: * Fisher logs actual catch on return.
7: * If catch >15 kg per trip, excess is returned to communal **reserve** and recorded in the **ledger**.
8: * If weekly total >30 kg, excess is similarly returned.
9: * A single failure to report or breach triggers a **5 kg penalty** deposited to the reserve and logged.
10: * The **keeper** role rotates weekly, enforces limits, records penalties, and posts ledger entries.
11: * Repeated violations (two within 30 days) cause a forfeited free trip, logged in the ledger.
12: 
13: ## New Institutional Objects
14: * **reserve** – type `reserve.json`, holds a `balance` field (float, default 0). Allows deposits by all agents, no withdrawals.
15: * **ledger** – type `ledger.json`, holds an `entries` list. Supports `append` and `read` for all agents.
16: 
17: ## Object Instances
18: ```json
19: [
20:   {"id": "reserve", "type": "reserve"},
21:   {"id": "ledger", "type": "ledger"}
22: ]
23: ```

25: ## New Role
26: * **keeper** – exclusive weekly role, description *"weekly keeper for enforcing limits"*. Assigned by `KeeperAssignmentRule`.

32: | `actions/rules/harvest/penalty_rule.py` | `penalty_rule` | On any breach or failure to report, deposits a 5 kg penalty to reserve and logs it. |
33: | `actions/rules/harvest/keeper_assignment_rule.py` | `keeper_assignment_rule` | Rotates the exclusive `keeper` role weekly and records the assignment. |
34: | `actions/rules/harvest/repeated_violation_rule.py` | `repeated_violation_rule` | Detects two violations within 30 days and logs a forfeited free‑trip entry in the ledger. |

class KeeperAssignmentRule(Rule):
    type_name = "keeper_assignment_rule"

    def after_action(self, ctx, round_record):
        # Rotate keeper weekly (assuming each round is a day)
        if ctx.round_number % 7 == 0:
            # Choose next keeper randomly among alive fishers
            alive = [aid for aid, a in ctx.state["agents"].items() if a.get("alive", True)]
            if not alive:
                return
            # Simple rotation: pick next in list based on previous keeper
            prev = ctx.state.get("runtime", {}).get("keeper_last", None)
            if prev and prev in alive:
                idx = alive.index(prev)
                next_idx = (idx + 1) % len(alive)
                new_keeper = alive[next_idx]
            else:
                new_keeper = random.choice(alive)
            # Assign exclusive keeper role
            assign_role("keeper", new_keeper, ctx.fluents, ctx.round_number, exclusive=True,
                       narration="New weekly keeper assigned.")
            # End previous keeper's role if exists
            if prev:
                end_fact(ctx.fluents, "keeper", [], ctx.round_number,
                         narration="Keeper term ended.")
            # Store for next rotation
            ctx.state.setdefault("runtime", {})["keeper_last"] = new_keeper
        return None","lineStart":1,"lineEnd":32,"totalLines":32,"truncated":false}},"title":"actions/rules/harvest/keeper_assignment_rule.py","time":{"start":1789533181791,"end":1789533181800}},"id":"prt_0a87d575300104FNmFV5dLc9mA","sessionID":"ses_f57830cddffenUGVz3NPe2QDfL","messageID":"msg_0a87d51d4001JEyURe8i9zy4t8"}}

150	    """Reads the real `steps:` cap straight from the opencode agent's own

154	    regex, not a YAML parse — PyYAML isn't a project dependency (checked

156	    in the minimal HPC venv, so pulling one in just to read a single
157	    top-level integer field isn't worth the new dependency. Falls back to
158	    `default` on any read/parse failure, same "telemetry degrades, doesn't
159	    block" contract as the rest of this module."""

162	        match = re.search(r"^steps:\s*(\d+)", text, re.MULTILINE)

33	def catch_from_effort(effort, stock_kg):
34	    """Linear Schaefer-style catch equation (catch = effort x stock x
35	    catchability), matching Gupta et al.'s CPRAgent.harvest(). effort is
36	    the agent's own [0.0, 1.0] fishing-intensity choice; HARVEST_PRODUCTIVITY
37	    is their catchability coefficient q."""
38	    return effort * stock_kg * HARVEST_PRODUCTIVITY

41	def apply_regrowth(stock_kg):
42	    """Logistic growth on the leftover (post-harvest) stock — matches
43	    Gupta et al.'s CPRModel.step():
44	    ΔR = growth_rate * R * (1 - R/capacity), applied to what's left after
45	    harvest, not a flat per-round add. Growth slows as the stock nears
46	    carrying capacity and (unlike a flat add) can't outrun a depleted lake."""
47	    grown = stock_kg + GROWTH_RATE * stock_kg * (1 - stock_kg / CARRYING_CAPACITY_KG)
48	    return min(grown, CARRYING_CAPACITY_KG)
49

52	    """Running per-agent balance: this trip's catch in, the fixed
53	    consumption cost out — matches Gupta et al.'s CPRAgent.harvest():
54	    self.payoff += harvest_amount; self.payoff -= self.model.consumption.
55	    Unlike catch/regrowth this isn't about the lake at all — it's whether
56	    a fisher can keep feeding themselves from what they bring in."""
57	    return payoff + harvested_kg - CONSUMPTION_KG

1: # Round 1 Institutional Design Specification
2: 
3: ## Overview
4: Implemented the policy:
5: * Fisher records name, date, expected take before departing.
6: * Fisher logs actual catch on return.
7: * If catch >15 kg per trip, excess is returned to communal **reserve** and recorded in the **ledger**.
8: * If weekly total >30 kg, excess is similarly returned.
9: * A single failure to report or breach triggers a **5 kg penalty** deposited to the reserve and logged.
10: * The **keeper** role rotates weekly, enforces limits, records penalties, and posts ledger entries.
11: * Repeated violations (two within 30 days) cause a forfeited free trip, logged in the ledger.
12: 
13: ## New Institutional Objects
14: * **reserve** – type `reserve.json`, holds a `balance` field (float, default 0). Allows deposits by all agents, no withdrawals.
15: * **ledger** – type `ledger.json`, holds an `entries` list. Supports `append` and `read` for all agents.
16: 
17: ## Object Instances
18: ```json
19: [
20:   {"id": "reserve", "type": "reserve"},
21:   {"id": "ledger", "type": "ledger"}
22: ]
23: ```
24: 
25: ## New Role
26: * **keeper** – exclusive weekly role, description *"weekly keeper for enforcing limits"*. Assigned by `KeeperAssignmentRule`.
27: 
28: ## New Rules (Level 3) attached to `harvest`
29: | Rule File | type_name | Purpose |
30: |-----------|-----------|---------|
31: | `actions/rules/harvest/excess_return_rule.py` | `excess_return_rule` | Handles per‑trip (>15 kg) and weekly (>30 kg) excess returns, updates reserve and ledger, tracks weekly totals and violation rounds. |

from roles.roles import set_fact, end_fact
from engine.institution.agent_loop import per_agent_decision
from engine.physics import (
    catch_from_effort,
    apply_regrowth,
    apply_consumption,
    is_dead,
    available_stock,
    CARRYING_CAPACITY_KG,
)


def run(ctx):
    state = ctx.state
    runtime = state["runtime"]
    fluents = state["fluents"]
    round_number = ctx.round_number

    runtime.setdefault("payoff", {})
    runtime.setdefault("dead_agents", [])
    stock_before = available_stock(runtime)

    def build_fields(agent_id):
        constraints_line = ctx.rules.describe_constraints(ctx, agent_id)
        return {
            "stock_kg": stock_before,
            "carrying_capacity_kg": CARRYING_CAPACITY_KG,
            "constraints_line": f" {constraints_line}" if constraints_line else "",
            "stock_trend": _stock_trend(runtime, state["config"], round_number),
        }

    def build_record(agent_id, response):
        effort = min(1.0, max(0.0, float(response["effort"])))
        raw_kg = catch_from_effort(effort, stock_before)
        return {"effort": effort, "harvested_kg": raw_kg, "reasoning": response.get("reasoning", ""), "note": None}

    def after_settle(agent_id, record_entry):
        new_payoff = apply_consumption(runtime["payoff"].get(agent_id, 0.0), record_entry["harvested_kg"])
        runtime["payoff"][agent_id] = new_payoff
        if is_dead(new_payoff):
            runtime["dead_agents"].append(agent_id)
            name = state["agents"][agent_id]["name"]
            set_fact(
                fluents, "dead", [agent_id], agent_id, round_number,
                narration=f"{name} has died — they hadn't been catching enough fish to survive.",
                visibility="public",
            )
            end_fact(fluents, "fisher", [agent_id], round_number)

    def ineligible_record(agent_id):
        return {
            "effort": None, "harvested_kg": 0.0, "reasoning": "",
            "note": ctx.rules.ineligibility_note(ctx, agent_id), "participated": False,
        }

    agent_records = per_agent_decision(
        ctx, build_fields, build_record, ineligible_record=ineligible_record, after_settle=after_settle,
    )

    stock_after_harvest = stock_before - sum(r["harvested_kg"] for r in agent_records.values())
    stock_after_regrowth = apply_regrowth(stock_after_harvest)
    runtime["stock_kg"] = stock_after_regrowth

    # A rule that needs to override the round's own final stock number
    # (a "replenish the lake" trigger, say) does so from its own
    # after_action(ctx, round_record) hook — called generically by
    # ActionRuntime right after this function returns — by writing
    # ctx.state["runtime"]["stock_kg"] and round_record["stock_kg_after_regrowth"]
    # directly; no special override method is needed here for that.
    return {
        "agents": agent_records,
        "stock_kg_before": stock_before,
        "stock_kg_after_harvest": stock_after_harvest,
        "stock_kg_after_regrowth": stock_after_regrowth,
    }


def _stock_trend(runtime, config, round_number):
    """A short recent-history readout of surveyed stock levels, oldest to
    most recent — lets a fisher notice for themselves whether the lake has
    been recovering or shrinking, mirroring Gupta et al.'s CPRAgent prompt's

53	class ActionRuntime:
54	    @staticmethod
55	    def run_action(spec, state, round_number):
56	        """Builds the ActionContext, dispatches to the resolved handler,
57	        and appends the result to state["runtime"]["rounds"] — a handler
58	        returns the round_record's own content; "round"/"action" are
59	        filled in here if the handler didn't already set them, so a
60	        handler never has to repeat that boilerplate. Wraps the handler
61	        call with this action's own RuleSet.before_action()/after_action()
62	        — generic, identical for every action, whether or not anything is
63	        actually configured to attach to it this round (an empty RuleSet's
64	        before_action()/after_action() are no-ops)."""
65	        ctx = ActionContext.build(spec, state, round_number)
66	        handler = resolve_handler(spec["execution"]["handler"])
67	
68	        ctx.rules.before_action(ctx)
69	        round_record = handler(ctx)
70	        ctx.rules.after_action(ctx, round_record)
71	
72	        round_record.setdefault("round", round_number)
73	        round_record.setdefault("action", spec["name"])
74	
75	        runtime = state["runtime"]
76	        runtime["round"] = round_number
77	        runtime["rounds"].append(round_record)
78	        return round_record

# Skill: understand

# /understand

Analyze the current codebase and produce a `knowledge-graph.json` file in the project's data directory (`.ua/`, or the legacy `.understand-anything/` when it already exists). This file powers the interactive dashboard for exploring the project's architecture.

## Options

- `$ARGUMENTS` may contain:
  - `--full` — Force a full rebuild, ignoring any existing graph
  - `--auto-update` — Enable automatic graph updates on commit (writes `autoUpdate: true` to `$UA_DIR/config.json`)
  - `--no-auto-update` — Disable automatic graph updates (writes `autoUpdate: false` to `$UA_DIR/config.json`)
  - `--review` — Run full LLM graph-reviewer instead of inline deterministic validation
  - `--language <lang>` — Generate all textual content (summaries, descriptions, tags, titles, languageNotes, languageLesson) in the specified language. Accepts ISO 639-1 codes (`zh`, `ja`, `ko`, `en`, `es`, `fr`, `de`, etc.) or friendly names (`chinese`, `japanese`, `korean`, `english`, `spanish`, etc.). Locale variants supported: `zh-TW`, `zh-HK`, etc. Defaults to `en` (English). Stores preference in `$UA_DIR/config.json` for consistency across incremental updates.
  - `--exclude <patterns>` — Comma-separated glob patterns for additional files/directories to exclude from analysis (e.g., `--exclude "tests/*,docs/*"`). These patterns take highest priority over built-in defaults and `.understandignore` rules. Supports gitignore syntax including `!` negation.
  - A directory path (e.g. `/path/to/repo` or `../other-project`) — Analyze the given directory instead of the current working directory

---

## Progress Reporting

Throughout execution, report progress to the user at each phase transition and during batch processing. This keeps users informed on large codebases where analysis can take a long time.

- **Phase transitions:** At the start of each phase, print a status line:
  > `[Phase N/7] <phase name>...`
  >
  > Example: `[Phase 2/7] Analyzing files (12 batches)...`

- **Batch progress:** During Phase 2, report each batch with its index and total:
  > `Analyzing batch X/N (files: foo.ts, bar.ts, ...)` (list up to 3 filenames, then `...` if more)

- **Phase completion:** When a phase finishes, briefly confirm:
  > `Phase N complete. <one-line summary of result>`
  >
  > Example: `Phase 1 complete. Found 247 files across 3 languages.`

## Phase 0 — Pre-flight

Determine whether to run a full analysis or incremental update.

1. **Resolve `PROJECT_ROOT`:**
   - Parse `$ARGUMENTS` for a non-flag token (any argument that does not start with `--`). If found, treat it as the target directory path.
     - If the path is relative, resolve it against the current working directory.
     - Verify the resolved path exists and is a directory (run `test -d <path>`). If it does not exist or is not a directory, report an error to the user and **STOP**.
     - Set `PROJECT_ROOT` to the resolved absolute path.
   - If no directory path argument is found, set `PROJECT_ROOT` to the current working directory.
   - **Worktree redirect.** If `PROJECT_ROOT` is inside a git worktree (not the main checkout), redirect output to the main repository root. Worktrees managed by Claude Code are ephemeral — the data directory (`.ua/`, or legacy `.understand-anything/`) written there is destroyed when the session ends, taking the knowledge graph with it (issue #133). Detect a worktree by comparing `git rev-parse --git-dir` against `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`; in a normal checkout or submodule they resolve to the same path, in a worktree they differ and the parent of `--git-common-dir` is the main repo root.

     ```bash
     COMMON_DIR=$(git -C "$PROJECT_ROOT" rev-parse --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null)
     GIT_DIR=$(git -C "$PROJECT_ROOT" rev-parse --git-dir 2>/dev/null)
     if [ -n "$COMMON_DIR" ] && [ -n "$GIT_DIR" ]; then
       COMMON_ABS=$(cd "$PROJECT_ROOT" && cd "$COMMON_DIR" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
       GIT_ABS=$(cd "$PROJECT_ROOT" && cd "$GIT_DIR" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
       if [ -n "$COMMON_ABS" ] && [ "$COMMON_ABS" != "$GIT_ABS" ]; then
         MAIN_ROOT=$(dirname "$COMMON_ABS")
         if [ -d "$MAIN_ROOT" ] && [ "${UNDERSTAND_NO_WORKTREE_REDIRECT:-0}" != "1" ]; then
           echo "[understand] Detected git worktree at $PROJECT_ROOT"
           echo "[understand] Redirecting output to main repo root: $MAIN_ROOT"
           echo "[understand] (Set UNDERSTAND_NO_WORKTREE_REDIRECT=1 to keep PROJECT_ROOT as the worktree.)"
           PROJECT_ROOT="$MAIN_ROOT"
         fi
       fi
     fi
     ```

     Set `UNDERSTAND_NO_WORKTREE_REDIRECT=1` if you intentionally want a per-worktree graph (rare — most users want the redirect).

     "$COPILOT_SELF_RELATIVE" \

   if [ -z "$PLUGIN_ROOT" ]; then

     echo "Checked:"
     echo "  - ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-<unset CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT>}"
     echo "  - $HOME/.understand-anything-plugin"

     echo "  - $HOME/understand-anything/understand-anything-plugin"

#### Default path (no `--review`): inline deterministic validation

Write the following Node.js script to `$UA_DIR/tmp/ua-inline-validate.cjs`:

```javascript
#!/usr/bin/env node
const fs = require('fs');
const graphPath = process.argv[2];
const outputPath = process.argv[3];
try {
  const graph = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(graphPath, 'utf8'));
  const issues = [], warnings = [];
  if (!Array.isArray(graph.nodes)) { issues.push('graph.nodes is missing or not an array'); graph.nodes = []; }
  if (!Array.isArray(graph.edges)) { issues.push('graph.edges is missing or not an array'); graph.edges = []; }
  const nodeIds = new Set();
  const seen = new Map();
  graph.nodes.forEach((n, i) => {
    if (!n.id) { issues.push(`Node[${i}] missing id`); return; }
    if (!n.type) issues.push(`Node[${i}] '${n.id}' missing type`);
    if (!n.name) issues.push(`Node[${i}] '${n.id}' missing name`);
    if (!n.summary) issues.push(`Node[${i}] '${n.id}' missing summary`);
    if (!n.tags || !n.tags.length) issues.push(`Node[${i}] '${n.id}' missing tags`);
    if (seen.has(n.id)) issues.push(`Duplicate node ID '${n.id}' at indices ${seen.get(n.id)} and ${i}`);
    else seen.set(n.id, i);
    nodeIds.add(n.id);
  });
  graph.edges.forEach((e, i) => {
    if (!nodeIds.has(e.source)) issues.push(`Edge[${i}] source '${e.source}' not found`);
    if (!nodeIds.has(e.target)) issues.push(`Edge[${i}] target '${e.target}' not found`);
  });
  const fileLevelTypes = new Set(['file', 'config', 'document', 'service', 'pipeline', 'table', 'schema', 'resource', 'endpoint']);
  const fileNodes = graph.nodes.filter(n => fileLevelTypes.has(n.type)).map(n => n.id);
  const assigned = new Map();
  if (!Array.isArray(graph.layers)) { if (graph.layers) warnings.push('graph.layers is not an array'); graph.layers = []; }
  if (!Array.isArray(graph.tour)) { if (graph.tour) warnings.push('graph.tour is not an array'); graph.tour = []; }
  graph.layers.forEach(layer => {
    (layer.nodeIds || []).forEach(id => {
      if (!nodeIds.has(id)) issues.push(`Layer '${layer.id}' refs missing node '${id}'`);
      if (assigned.has(id)) issues.push(`Node '${id}' appears in multiple layers`);
      assigned.set(id, layer.id);
    });
  });
  fileNodes.forEach(id => {
    if (!assigned.has(id)) issues.push(`File node '${id}' not in any layer`);
  });
  graph.tour.forEach((step, i) => {
    (step.nodeIds || []).forEach(id => {
      if (!nodeIds.has(id)) issues.push(`Tour step[${i}] refs missing node '${id}'`);
    });
  });
  const withEdges = new Set([
    ...graph.edges.map(e => e.source),
    ...graph.edges.map(e => e.target)
  ]);
  graph.nodes.forEach(n => {
    if (!withEdges.has(n.id)) warnings.push(`Node '${n.id}' has no edges (orphan)`);
  });
  const stats = {
    totalNodes: graph.nodes.length,
    totalEdges: graph.edges.length,
    totalLayers: graph.layers.length,
    tourSteps: graph.tour.length,
    nodeTypes: graph.nodes.reduce((a, n) => { a[n.type] = (a[n.type]||0)+1; return a; }, {}),
    edgeTypes: graph.edges.reduce((a, e) => { a[e.type] = (a[e.type]||0)+1; return a; }, {})
  };
  fs.writeFileSync(outputPath, JSON.stringify({ issues, warnings, stats }, null, 2));
  process.exit(0);
} catch (err) { process.stderr.write(err.message + '\n'); process.exit(1); }
```

3. Write metadata to `$UA_DIR/meta.json` (only after step 2 succeeded):
   ```json
   {
     "lastAnalyzedAt": "<ISO 8601 timestamp>",
     "gitCommitHash": "<commit hash>",
     "version": "1.0.0",
     "analyzedFiles": <number of files analyzed>
   }
   ```

4. Clean up intermediate files, **preserving `scan-result.json`** so future incremental runs can skip Phase 1 SCAN (see issue #293). We `mv` scratch dirs into a timestamped `.trash-*` instead of `rm -rf`ing them directly — this avoids tripping destructive-action gates on hardened hosts (e.g. freshness-window checks) that flag deleting directories created moments earlier (see issue #301). The delayed-purge step in Phase 0 reclaims the space once the trash is older than 7 days.
   ```bash
   # Preserve scan-result.json — Phase 1's deterministic file inventory.
   # Future incremental runs (Phase 2 compute-batches.mjs --changed-files=…)
   # need this inventory; without it, Phase 1 must re-dispatch and pay ~157k
   # tokens / ~158s per incremental run.
   TRASH="$UA_DIR/.trash-$(date +%s)"
   mkdir -p "$TRASH"
   INTER="$UA_DIR/intermediate"
   if [ -d "$INTER" ]; then
     # Move every entry except scan-result.json into the trash dir.
     find "$INTER" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -not -name 'scan-result.json' -exec mv {} "$TRASH/" \; 2>/dev/null || true
   fi
   mv "$UA_DIR/tmp" "$TRASH/" 2>/dev/null || true
   ```

5. Report a summary to the user containing:
   - Project name and description
   - Files analyzed / total files (with breakdown by fileCategory: code, config, docs, infra, data, script, markup)
   - Nodes created (broken down by type: file, function, class, config, document, service, table, endpoint, pipeline, schema, resource)
   - Edges created (broken down by type)
   - Layers identified (with names)
   - Tour steps generated (count)
   - Any warnings from the reviewer
   - Path to the output file: `$UA_DIR/knowledge-graph.json`

6. Only automatically launch the dashboard by invoking the `/understand-dashboard` skill if final graph validation passed after normalization/review fixes.
   If final validation did not pass, report that the graph was saved with warnings and dashboard launch was skipped.

- ALWAYS save partial results — a partial graph is better than no graph.

3:  * scan-project.mjs
4:  *
5:  * Deterministic file enumeration + language/category detection for the
6:  * project-scanner agent. Replaces the LLM-written prose scanner that used to
7:  * (a) author a per-run Node.js script (`tmp/ua-project-scan.js`), (b) walk the
8:  * file tree, and (c) classify each file via lookup tables in LLM context — a
9:  * pure rule-lookup pass that was being billed at LLM rates and adding many
10:  * minutes of per-run latency on mid-sized monorepos.
11:  *
12:  * What the LLM still owns (Step A of project-scanner.md Phase 1):
13:  *   - Reading README + top-level manifests to synthesize `name`,
14:  *     `rawDescription`, `readmeHead`, `frameworks`, and the high-level
15:  *     `languages` narrative.
16:  *
17:  * What this script owns:
18:  *   - File enumeration (git ls-files preferred, recursive walk fallback)
19:  *   - `.understandignore` and CLI exclusion filtering (delegated to core's
20:  *     createIgnoreFilter, which reads the resolved data dir — `.ua/`, or
21:  *     legacy `.understand-anything/` when that directory already exists)
22:  *   - Per-file language detection (extension + filename table)

27:  *

30:  *     [--exclude <patterns>] [--exclude-analysis-data]
31:  *
32:  *   --exclude <patterns>  Comma-separated gitignore-style patterns to
33:  *                         additionally exclude from the scan.

35:  *                            `.understand-anything/` analysis data.

39:  * produce the final scan-result.json):

56:  * comparison before emission. The content digest uses that same order and

228: /**
229:  * Detect the language of a file by its path. Lowercase extension lookup,
230:  * then no-extension filename lookup. Never returns null — falls back to
231:  * the lowercased extension (without dot) or 'unknown' if there is no
232:  * extension. Downstream consumers rely on this field always being a string
233:  * (see project-scanner.md Step 3 "Fallback" note).
234:  */
235: export function detectLanguage(filePath) {
236:   const base = basename(filePath);
237:   const ext = extname(filePath).toLowerCase();
238: 
239:   // Dockerfile.dev, Dockerfile.prod, etc. — common variant form.
240:   if (base === 'Dockerfile' || base.startsWith('Dockerfile.')) return 'dockerfile';
241: 
242:   // Dotfile names like .env, .env.local — path.extname returns '' for
243:   // single-segment dotfiles (e.g. '.env') and the SECOND segment for

245:   // intended LANGUAGE_BY_EXT['.env'] mapping. Try the leading dotfile
246:   // portion first so `.env`, `.env.local`, `.env.production` all map.
247:   const dotKey = dotfileKey(base);
248:   if (dotKey && LANGUAGE_BY_EXT[dotKey]) return LANGUAGE_BY_EXT[dotKey];
249: 
250:   if (ext) {
251:     const byExt = LANGUAGE_BY_EXT[ext];
252:     if (byExt) return byExt;

254:     return ext.slice(1);
255:   }

257:   // No-extension file — try filename table.

278:   if (!base.startsWith('.')) return null;
279:   const m = base.match(/^(\.[a-z0-9]+)/i);
280:   return m ? m[1].toLowerCase() : null;
281: }
282: 
283: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
284: // Category detection
285: //
286: // Implements the priority-ordered rules from project-scanner.md Step 4.
287: // Order matters: more specific rules must run before more general ones
288: // (e.g. `docker-compose.yml` is infra, not config).
289: //
290: // Categories: code | config | docs | infra | data | script | markup
291: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
292: 
293: /**
294:  * Extension -> category. Used only after the higher-priority path-based
295:  * checks (infra/docs exclusions) in `detectCategory()`. Plain extension
296:  * lookup is intentionally last-resort — many configs need their full path
297:  * inspected first.
298:  */
299: const CATEGORY_BY_EXT = Object.freeze({
300:   // docs
301:   '.md': 'docs',
302:   '.mdx': 'docs',
303:   '.rst': 'docs',
304:   '.txt': 'docs',
305:   '.text': 'docs',
306:   // config
307:   '.yaml': 'config',
308:   '.yml': 'config',
309:   '.json': 'config',
310:   '.jsonc': 'config',
311:   '.toml': 'config',
312:   '.xml': 'config',
313:   '.xsl': 'config',
314:   '.xsd': 'config',
315:   '.plist': 'config',
316:   '.cfg': 'config',
317:   '.ini': 'config',
318:   '.env': 'config',
319:   '.properties': 'config',
320:   '.csproj': 'config',
321:   '.sln': 'config',
322:   '.mod': 'config',
323:   '.sum': 'config',
324:   '.gradle': 'config',
325:   '.sbt': 'config',
326:   // infra
327:   '.tf': 'infra',
328:   '.tfvars': 'infra',
329:   // data
330:   '.sql': 'data',
331:   '.graphql': 'data',
332:   '.gql': 'data',
333:   '.proto': 'data',
334:   '.prisma': 'data',
335:   '.csv': 'data',
336:   '.tsv': 'data',
337:   // script
338:   '.sh': 'script',
339:   '.bash': 'script',
340:   '.zsh': 'script',
341:   '.ps1': 'script',
342:   '.psm1': 'script',
343:   '.psd1': 'script',
344:   '.bat': 'script',
345:   '.cmd': 'script',
346:   // markup
347:   '.html': 'markup',
348:   '.htm': 'markup',
349:   '.css': 'markup',
350:   '.scss': 'markup',
351:   '.sass': 'markup',
352:   '.less': 'markup',
353: });
354: 
355: /**
356:  * Filenames (no extension or full filename with extension) that always
357:  * map to `infra` regardless of their extension. Compared case-sensitively
358:  * against basename(path).
359:  */
360: const INFRA_FILENAMES = new Set([
361:   'Dockerfile',
362:   '.dockerignore',
363:   'Makefile',
364:   'GNUmakefile',
365:   'makefile',
366:   'Jenkinsfile',
367:   'Procfile',
368:   'Vagrantfile',
369:   '.gitlab-ci.yml',
370: ]);
371: 
372: /**
373:  * Detect the project-scanner category for a file. Priority order matches
374:  * project-scanner.md Step 4 "Priority rule" — most specific wins.
375:  *
376:  * 1. LICENSE -> code (per the spec note "except LICENSE"). The Step-2
377:  *    exclusion table normally removes LICENSE, but if a project chooses to
378:  *    re-include it via `.understandignore` negation, it should NOT land in
379:  *    docs. We classify as `code` rather than inventing a new bucket.
380:  * 2. Filename-based infra (Dockerfile, Makefile, Jenkinsfile,
381:  *    docker-compose.*, Vagrantfile, Procfile, .gitlab-ci.yml,
382:  *    .dockerignore).
383:  * 3. Path-based infra (.github/workflows/, .circleci/, k8s/, kubernetes/,
384:  *    *.k8s.yml, *.k8s.yaml).
385:  * 4. Extension-based mapping (CATEGORY_BY_EXT).
386:  * 5. Fallback: `code` (matches the spec — "All other extensions").
387:  */
388: export function detectCategory(filePath) {
389:   const base = basename(filePath);
390:   const ext = extname(filePath).toLowerCase();
391:   const posix = filePath.split(sep).join('/');
392: 
393:   // Rule 1: LICENSE exception (project-scanner.md Step 4 table comment).
394:   if (base === 'LICENSE') return 'code';
395: 
396:   // Rule 2: infra by filename — Dockerfile + variants, Makefile,
397:   // Jenkinsfile, docker-compose.*, Procfile, Vagrantfile, .gitlab-ci.yml,
398:   // .dockerignore.
399:   if (INFRA_FILENAMES.has(base)) return 'infra';
400:   if (base === 'Dockerfile' || base.startsWith('Dockerfile.')) return 'infra';
401:   if (base.startsWith('docker-compose.')) return 'infra';
402:   if (base === 'compose.yml' || base === 'compose.yaml') return 'infra';
403: 
404:   // Rule 3: infra by path.
405:   if (posix.startsWith('.github/workflows/')) return 'infra';
406:   if (posix.startsWith('.circleci/')) return 'infra';
407:   // Match a `k8s/` or `kubernetes/` segment anywhere in the path.
408:   if (/(^|\/)(k8s|kubernetes)\//.test(posix)) return 'infra';
409:   // `*.k8s.yml` and `*.k8s.yaml` — Kubernetes-flavored YAML.
410:   if (/\.k8s\.(ya?ml)$/i.test(base)) return 'infra';
411: 
412:   // Rule 4: extension-based lookup.
413:   if (ext) {
414:     const byExt = CATEGORY_BY_EXT[ext];
415:     if (byExt) return byExt;
416:   }
417: 
418:   // Rule 4.5: dotfile-style configs (.env, .env.local, .env.production).
419:   // path.extname misses these — see dotfileKey docstring.
420:   const dotKey = dotfileKey(base);
421:   if (dotKey) {
422:     const byDot = CATEGORY_BY_EXT[dotKey];
423:     if (byDot) return byDot;
424:   }
425: 
426:   // Rule 5: filename-based config catch-all for no-extension config files
427:   // commonly seen in JVM/Go/.NET projects (covered above for infra but not
428:   // config). We don't enumerate every possible config filename here — that
429:   // gets handled by the language map's no-extension entries upstream.
430:   // Anything not matched falls through to `code`.
431:   return 'code';
432: }

434: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
435: // Complexity estimation (project-scanner.md Step 7)
436: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
437: 
438: /**
439:  * Map a total file count to a complexity tier. Thresholds are inclusive on
440:  * the lower bound:
441:  *   - small:      1-30
442:  *   - moderate:   31-150
443:  *   - large:      151-500
444:  *   - very-large: >500
445:  *
446:  * Edge case: 0 files maps to `small` (the lowest tier) so the field is
447:  * always set even on empty repos. Downstream consumers treat 0 files as
448:  * a sentinel for "nothing to analyze" via `totalFiles`, not complexity.
449:  */
450: export function estimateComplexity(totalFiles) {
451:   if (totalFiles <= 30) return 'small';
452:   if (totalFiles <= 150) return 'moderate';
453:   if (totalFiles <= 500) return 'large';
454:   return 'very-large';
455: }
456: 
457: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
458: // File enumeration
459: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
460: 
461: /**
462:  * Normalize a path to forward-slash POSIX. The project-scanner contract
463:  * emits POSIX paths; we re-normalize so the output is stable across
464:  * Windows/macOS/Linux.
465:  */
466: function toPosix(p) {
467:   return p.split(sep).join('/');
468: }
469: 
470: /**
471:  * Locale-independent string order. ECMAScript relational string comparison
472:  * is lexicographic over UTF-16 code units, so the result cannot vary with ICU,
473:  * process locale, or operating system settings.
474:  */
475: function compareStableStrings(a, b) {
476:   if (a < b) return -1;
477:   if (a > b) return 1;
478:   return 0;
479: }
480: 
481: /**
482:  * Enumerate all files in `projectRoot` via `git ls-files`. Returns an
483:  * array of project-relative POSIX paths, or null if the directory is not
484:  * a git repository (or git is not installed). Caller falls back to the
485:  * recursive walker.
486:  *
487:  * Why git ls-files first: it respects the repo's `.gitignore`, handles
488:  * submodules sensibly, and gives a fast, deterministic listing. The walker
489:  * is a strict superset of what git would emit (no .gitignore awareness),
490:  * so the ignore filter has to do more work in the fallback path.
491:  */
492: function enumerateViaGit(projectRoot) {
493:   // -z = NUL-terminated output. Without it, `git ls-files` C-escapes non-ASCII
494:   // bytes in path names — paths containing emoji, accented characters, CJK
495:   // codepoints, etc. come back quoted with octal escapes (e.g.
496:   // `"30. \360\237\217\227 BD-CCER/file.md"` for a path containing 🏗️).
497:   // Those quoted-escaped strings then fail to round-trip back to real disk
498:   // paths in downstream consumers, so files in such directories are silently
499:   // dropped from the scan. The -z form emits raw bytes between NUL separators,
500:   // preserving every codepoint as-is. This is the same approach git itself
501:   // uses for `--null` everywhere downstream (xargs -0, etc.).
502:   const result = spawnSync('git', ['ls-files', '-z', '-co', '--exclude-standard'], {
503:     cwd: projectRoot,
504:     encoding: 'utf-8',
505:     maxBuffer: 256 * 1024 * 1024, // 256MB — huge monorepos can produce >10MB of paths
506:   });
507:   if (result.status !== 0 || !result.stdout) return null;
508:   // Each NUL-separated chunk is one path, project-relative, already POSIX on
509:   // all platforms because git emits forward slashes regardless of OS.
510:   return result.stdout
511:     .split('\0')
512:     .filter(Boolean)
513:     .map(toPosix);
514: }
515: 
516: /**
517:  * Recursive directory walker — fallback when `git ls-files` is unavailable
518:  * (no git, not a repo, or git refused). Skips hard-coded "obviously bad"
519:  * directory names BEFORE invoking the ignore filter so we don't waste cycles
520:  * descending into `node_modules/` etc. on huge trees.
521:  *
522:  * Yields project-relative POSIX paths in directory-sorted order so the
523:  * output is deterministic without an extra sort pass.
524:  */
525: function enumerateViaWalk(projectRoot) {
526:   // Hard skip — these directories are universally non-source and skipping
527:   // at the walker level avoids materializing thousands of node_modules
528:   // paths before the ignore filter drops them. The ignore filter still
529:   // runs on everything else.
530:   const HARD_SKIP_DIRS = new Set([
531:     'node_modules',
532:     '.git',
533:     '.svn',
534:     '.hg',
535:     '__pycache__',
536:   ]);
537: 
538:   const out = [];
539: 
540:   function walk(absDir) {
541:     let entries;
542:     try {
543:       entries = readdirSync(absDir, { withFileTypes: true });
544:     } catch (err) {
545:       process.stderr.write(
546:         `Warning: scan-project: ${toPosix(relative(projectRoot, absDir)) || '.'} ` +
547:         `— directory read failed (${err.message}) — subtree skipped\n`,
548:       );
549:       return;
550:     }
551:     // Sort deterministically by name; mix files and dirs together so the
552:     // final output (after the path sort) is identical regardless of
553:     // OS-specific readdir order.
554:     entries.sort((a, b) => compareStableStrings(a.name, b.name));
555:     for (const ent of entries) {
556:       if (ent.isDirectory()) {
557:         if (HARD_SKIP_DIRS.has(ent.name)) continue;
558:         walk(join(absDir, ent.name));
559:       } else if (ent.isFile()) {
560:         const rel = toPosix(relative(projectRoot, join(absDir, ent.name)));
561:         if (rel) out.push(rel);
562:       }
563:       // Symlinks intentionally ignored — git ls-files doesn't follow them
564:       // either, and following them is a classic recursion-bomb footgun.
565:     }
566:   }
567: 
568:   walk(projectRoot);
569:   return out;
570: }
571: 
572: /**
573:  * Enumerate all candidate files in `projectRoot`. Tries git ls-files first;
574:  * falls back to a recursive walk if git is unavailable or this is not a
575:  * repo. Returns an array of project-relative POSIX paths in unspecified
576:  * order — caller is responsible for sorting + filtering.
577:  */
578: function enumerateFiles(projectRoot) {
579:   const fromGit = enumerateViaGit(projectRoot);
580:   if (fromGit !== null) return fromGit;
581:   process.stderr.write(
582:     `scan-project: git ls-files unavailable — falling back to recursive walk\n`,
583:   );
584:   return enumerateViaWalk(projectRoot);
585: }
586: 
587: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
588: // Filter accounting
589: //
590: // The project-scanner.md contract requires `filteredByIgnore` to count files
591: // dropped specifically by user `.understandignore` or CLI `--exclude`
592: // patterns (the delta beyond what the hardcoded defaults would have removed).
593: // We accomplish this by building TWO filters:
594: //   - `defaultOnly`: defaults only, no user patterns
595: //   - `combined`: defaults + user patterns (createIgnoreFilter)
596: // and counting paths that the combined filter excludes but the defaults-only
597: // filter would have kept.
598: //
599: // Negation (`!pattern`) is correctly handled by the combined filter — a file
600: // re-included via `!` won't be in the combined-excluded set, so it WON'T be
601: // counted in filteredByIgnore (it's "kept", not "additionally filtered").
602: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
603: 
604: /**
605:  * Build a defaults-only IgnoreFilter — same patterns as createIgnoreFilter
606:  * would apply, minus any user .understandignore content. We synthesize this
607:  * via a temp directory with no .understandignore files so the core function
608:  * still drives the matcher. (Re-implementing the ignore-package wiring here
609:  * would risk subtle behavior drift from core's matcher.)
610:  */
611: function buildDefaultsOnlyFilter() {
612:   // Use the createIgnoreFilter with a path that we KNOW has no .understandignore.
613:   // `os.tmpdir()`-based fresh dir guarantees no user patterns leak in.
614:   // The directory doesn't need to exist on disk because createIgnoreFilter
615:   // only checks existsSync() before reading.
616:   const fakeProjectRoot = join(
617:     require('node:os').tmpdir(),
618:     `ua-scan-defaults-${process.pid}-${Date.now()}`,
619:   );
620:   return createIgnoreFilter(fakeProjectRoot);
621: }
622: 
623: /**
624:  * Determine whether `projectRoot` has any user .understandignore files.
625:  * When neither file exists, the combined and defaults-only filters are
626:  * identical, so we can skip the dual-filter accounting entirely.
627:  *
628:  * Mirrors core's createIgnoreFilter, which reads the resolved data dir —
629:  * `.ua/`, or legacy `.understand-anything/` when that directory already
630:  * exists (see resolveUaDir).
631:  */
632: function hasUserIgnoreFile(projectRoot) {
633:   return (
634:     existsSync(join(projectRoot, '.understandignore'))
635:     || existsSync(join(resolveUaDir(projectRoot), '.understandignore'))
636:   );
637: }
638: 
639: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
640: // Line counting
641: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
642: 
643: /**
644:  * Read a file once and count its newline-delimited lines. Returns both the raw
645:  * bytes and the number of `\n` characters; the caller feeds those same bytes
646:  * directly into the content digest without a second read or a whole-repo
647:  * content concatenation. The count matches `wc -l` semantics.
648:  *
649:  * Per-file failure: emits a Warning: and returns null. Caller decides
650:  * whether to drop the file or keep it with sizeLines=0.
651:  */
652: function readAndCountLines(absPath, posixPath) {
653:   try {
654:     const buf = readFileSync(absPath);
655:     // Manual newline count beats split('\n').length on large files — no
656:     // intermediate array allocation. We count the `\n` byte (0x0a) directly.
657:     let count = 0;
658:     for (let i = 0; i < buf.length; i++) {
659:       if (buf[i] === 0x0a) count++;
660:     }
661:     return { bytes: buf, sizeLines: count };
662:   } catch (err) {
663:     process.stderr.write(
664:       `Warning: scan-project: ${posixPath} — line count failed ` +
665:       `(${err.message}) — file skipped from output\n`,
666:     );
667:     return null;
668:   }
669: }
670: 
671: const CONTENT_DIGEST_DOMAIN = Buffer.from('understand-anything:scan-content:v1\0', 'utf-8');
672: 
673: /**
674:  * Add one scanned regular file to the aggregate fingerprint. Entries arrive
675:  * in compareStableStrings path order. Each frame is:
676:  *   uint32be(path UTF-8 byte length) || uint64be(content byte length) ||
677:  *   UTF-8 path bytes || raw content bytes
678:  * Length prefixes make path/content and adjacent-entry boundaries unambiguous.
679:  */
680: function updateContentDigest(hash, posixPath, contentBytes) {
681:   const pathBytes = Buffer.from(posixPath, 'utf-8');
682:   const lengths = Buffer.allocUnsafe(12);
683:   lengths.writeUInt32BE(pathBytes.length, 0);
684:   lengths.writeBigUInt64BE(BigInt(contentBytes.length), 4);
685:   hash.update(lengths);
686:   hash.update(pathBytes);
687:   hash.update(contentBytes);
688: }
689: 
690: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
691: // Main
692: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
693: 
694: async function main() {
695:   const args = process.argv.slice(2);
696:   let projectRoot;
697:   let outputPath;
698:   let excludeAnalysisData = false;
699:   const excludePatterns = [];
700: 
701:   for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i++) {
702:     const arg = args[i];
703:     if (arg === '--exclude-analysis-data') {
704:       excludeAnalysisData = true;
705:       continue;
706:     }
707:     if (arg === '--exclude') {
708:       const value = args[i + 1];
709:       if (!value || value.startsWith('--')) {
710:         process.stderr.write('scan-project.mjs failed: --exclude requires patterns\n');
711:         process.exit(1);
712:       }
713:       excludePatterns.push(
714:         ...value
715:           .split(',')
716:           .map(pattern => pattern.trim())
717:           .filter(Boolean),
718:       );
719:       i++;
720:       continue;
721:     }
722:     if (arg.startsWith('--')) {
723:       process.stderr.write(`scan-project.mjs failed: unknown option: ${arg}\n`);
724:       process.exit(1);
725:     }
726:     if (!projectRoot) {
727:       projectRoot = arg;
728:       continue;
729:     }
730:     if (!outputPath) {
731:       outputPath = arg;
732:       continue;
733:     }
734:     process.stderr.write(`scan-project.mjs failed: unexpected argument: ${arg}\n`);
735:     process.exit(1);
736:   }
737: 
738:   if (!projectRoot || !outputPath) {
739:     process.stderr.write(
740:       'Usage: node scan-project.mjs <projectRoot> <outputPath> ' +
741:       '[--exclude <patterns>] [--exclude-analysis-data]\n',
742:     );
743:     process.exit(1);
744:   }
745: 
746:   if (!existsSync(projectRoot)) {
747:     process.stderr.write(
748:       `scan-project.mjs failed: projectRoot does not exist: ${projectRoot}\n`,
749:     );
750:     process.exit(1);
751:   }
752:   const projectRootStat = statSync(projectRoot);
753:   if (!projectRootStat.isDirectory()) {
754:     process.stderr.write(
755:       `scan-project.mjs failed: projectRoot is not a directory: ${projectRoot}\n`,
756:     );
757:     process.exit(1);
758:   }
759: 
760:   // 1. Enumerate. Either git ls-files or recursive walk.
761:   const candidates = enumerateFiles(projectRoot).filter(
762:     rel =>
763:       !excludeAnalysisData ||
764:       (!rel.startsWith('.ua/') && !rel.startsWith('.understand-anything/')),
765:   );
766: 
767:   // 2. Filter via createIgnoreFilter (defaults + .understandignore + CLI excludes).
768:   //    Build a defaults-only filter in parallel to count user-driven drops.
769:   const combined = createIgnoreFilter(projectRoot, excludePatterns);
770:   const userIgnoresPresent = hasUserIgnoreFile(projectRoot) || excludePatterns.length > 0;
771:   const defaultsOnly = userIgnoresPresent ? buildDefaultsOnlyFilter() : combined;
772: 
773:   let filteredByIgnore = 0;
774:   const kept = [];
775:   for (const rel of candidates) {
776:     const isIgnoredCombined = combined.isIgnored(rel);
777:     if (!isIgnoredCombined) {
778:       kept.push(rel);
779:       continue;
780:     }
781:     // Dropped by combined filter. If defaults-only would have ALSO dropped
782:     // it, this is a baseline default drop — not counted. If defaults-only
783:     // would have KEPT it, this drop is attributable to the user's
784:     // .understandignore content or CLI --exclude patterns.
785:     if (userIgnoresPresent && !defaultsOnly.isIgnored(rel)) {
786:       filteredByIgnore++;
787:     }
788:   }
789: 
790:   // The per-file pass, output, stats key insertion, and content fingerprint
791:   // all consume this one locale-independent path order.
792:   kept.sort(compareStableStrings);
793: 
794:   // 3. Per-file: language + category + line count.
795:   //    Drop files that fail line counting (per-file resilience).
796:   const fileEntries = [];
797:   const contentHash = createHash('sha256');
798:   contentHash.update(CONTENT_DIGEST_DOMAIN);
799:   for (const rel of kept) {
800:     const absPath = join(projectRoot, rel);
801:     // lstat first so Git-enumerated symlinks are rejected before any operation
802:     // can follow them to a repository-external target.
803:     try {
804:       const st = lstatSync(absPath);
805:       if (st.isSymbolicLink()) {
806:         process.stderr.write(
807:           `Warning: scan-project: ${rel} — symbolic link skipped ` +
808:           `— file skipped from output\n`,
809:         );
810:         continue;
811:       }
812:       if (!st.isFile()) {
813:         // Directories and special files are not scanned as regular-file input.
814:         continue;
815:       }
816:     } catch (err) {
817:       process.stderr.write(
818:         `Warning: scan-project: ${rel} — lstat failed (${err.message}) ` +
819:         `— file skipped from output\n`,
820:       );
821:       continue;
822:     }
823:     const scanned = readAndCountLines(absPath, rel);
824:     if (scanned === null) {
825:       // readAndCountLines already emitted the Warning: line.
826:       continue;
827:     }
828:     updateContentDigest(contentHash, rel, scanned.bytes);
829:     fileEntries.push({
830:       path: rel,
831:       language: detectLanguage(rel),
832:       sizeLines: scanned.sizeLines,
833:       fileCategory: detectCategory(rel),
834:     });
835:   }
836: 
837:   // 4. Determinism: preserve the documented locale-independent path order.
838:   fileEntries.sort((a, b) => compareStableStrings(a.path, b.path));
839:   const contentDigest = contentHash.digest('hex');
840: 
841:   // 5. Stats.
842:   const byCategory = {};
843:   const byLanguage = {};
844:   for (const f of fileEntries) {
845:     byCategory[f.fileCategory] = (byCategory[f.fileCategory] || 0) + 1;
846:     byLanguage[f.language] = (byLanguage[f.language] || 0) + 1;
847:   }
848: 
849:   const estimatedComplexity = estimateComplexity(fileEntries.length);
850: 
851:   const output = {
852:     scriptCompleted: true,
853:     contentDigest,
854:     files: fileEntries,
855:     totalFiles: fileEntries.length,
856:     filteredByIgnore,
857:     estimatedComplexity,
858:     stats: {
859:       filesScanned: fileEntries.length,
860:       byCategory,
861:       byLanguage,
862:     },
863:   };
864: 
865:   writeFileSync(outputPath, JSON.stringify(output, null, 2), 'utf-8');
866: 
867:   if (!existsSync(outputPath)) {
868:     throw new Error(`output file missing after write: ${outputPath}`);
869:   }
870: 
871:   process.stderr.write(
872:     `scan-project: filesScanned=${fileEntries.length} ` +
873:     `filteredByIgnore=${filteredByIgnore} ` +
874:     `complexity=${estimatedComplexity}\n`,
875:   );
876: }

878: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
879: // Run only when executed directly as a CLI; importing the module (e.g. from
880: // tests) must not trigger main().
881: //
882: // Canonicalize both sides through realpathSync. Node ESM resolves
883: // import.meta.url through symlinks but pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]) preserves

  if (a > b) return 1;

 * descending into `node_modules/` etc. on huge trees.
